title: Heat links to severe coral bleaching were not established in all four Atlantic and Pacific samples in 2003-2019
abstract: We tested whether heat stress predicted a larger share of surveys with at least 50% coral bleaching at repeated sites. Four separate Atlantic and Pacific period models used 5,336 site-month records in 2003-2019. Three samples had severe cases and positive slopes. Only the later Pacific country-cluster interval was above zero after adjustment for four tests: +3.98 percentage points per four TSA degree-heating weeks, with an interval of +1.21 to +6.75. Its interval included zero with year or ecological-region clusters. The later Atlantic repeat-site sample had no severe cases; two severe records in the wider sample did not pass the repeat-year rule. Thus a clear severe-response link was not established in all four samples. Sparse severe events, limited heat support, missing surveys and error dependence limit inference. This is an observational support audit, not a causal climate-change or pollution test. Code, monthly evidence, source hashes, checks, all estimates and figures are included.

display.caption: Primary severe-survey share slopes. Thick lines show nominal intervals. Thin lines show four-test adjusted intervals. The later Atlantic sample has no severe cases and no interval.
Threshold checks by ocean and period. Bars show 1.96 country-cluster standard errors. These checks do not establish a preferred threshold.
